rows: Umar: intentions hadith. Ibn Umar: five pillars hadith

model.title: Explain why Muslims check the isnad of a hadith.

parts.text: Point: to make sure a report really comes from the Prophet ﷺ
Explain: checking each narrator's honesty and accuracy exposes mistakes and lies
Link: so Muslims follow only what is authentic

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A developed PEEL paragraph with a reference.

blocks.text: Answer from memory first. Then check your notes and correct in a different colour.

questions.q: What are the two main sources of Islam?
Which angel brought the Qur'an to the Prophet ﷺ?
Name one thing the Prophet ﷺ did that Muslims copy today.
questions.a: For example: saying Bismillah before eating, eating with the right hand, using a miswak

questions.q: Name the four main grades of hadith.
Which book begins with the hadith on intentions?

frame.label: Link
starters: This links to the question because

keywords.def: a report of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved
the way of the Prophet ﷺ: his sayings, actions and approvals
the chain of narrators who passed a hadith on
authentic: a reliable hadith that meets all the conditions
intention: the purpose in the heart
pillars: the main supports of Islam

questions.q: Write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain why the Sunnah is important.'
questions.a: Point: it explains the Qur'an. Evidence: 16:44 or 4:80. Explain: e.g. salah details. Link: Muslims need it to practise Islam.

questions.q: Fill the gap: a hadith with a liar in its chain is ...
Retrieval grid (pupil PDF): nine boxes, one question each from across the unit. Answer from memory first, then check your notes in a different colour.
questions.a: Answers from the unit: definitions, narrators, grades, conditions, pillars, ayat 4:80, 16:44, 49:6, 98:5.

questions.q: Extend: write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain why intentions matter in Islam.'
questions.a: Point, the intentions hadith with source, example, link.

questions.q: Stretch: 'Muslims should only ever share hadith that are sahih.' Give one reason to agree and one point to consider.
questions.a: Agree: lying about the Prophet ﷺ is very serious. Consider: hasan hadith are also accepted; the key is to share only what scholars accept and to cite the source.

questions.q: Which hadith did Abdullah ibn Umar narrate?
questions.a: A) Islam is built on five. Ibn Umar narrated the five pillars hadith. The intentions hadith is from his father, Umar; 'none of you truly believes' is from Anas.

questions.q: Think again: what would you most want a friend to know, and why?
questions.a: A reasoned point from the unit.
